rationale: Pulp's JavaScript bridge delivers one native pointer event through separate target and ancestor evaluate calls. Direct @pulp/react synthetic-event cancellation therefore needs a scoped internal token spanning that Pulp-specific bridge walk; without it, stopPropagation is discarded and native ancestor callbacks still fire. Pulp's later materialized-import integration also keeps the source application's QuickJS closures and hit behavior behind same-transaction DesignIR paint, captured typography, layout, and alternate-state atlases. These are Pulp-only Chromium, React bridge, and plugin-host concerns; a future Vellum importer should implement the same behavioral and visual parity contracts against its independent APIs rather than copy this integration.
